year_start.evidence: Landslide reactivations dated 2000 and April 2009; start year of any relocation not stated: 'Se ha reactivado en dos ocasiones, en el 2000 y 2009 (abril)'

households.evidence: Houses lost, not households moved: 'En abril del año 2009, según la información proveniente del Gobierno Regional de San Martín, colapsaron de 138 viviendas, locales religiosos y comunales.'

trigger.evidence: After the April 2009 landslide (138 houses collapsed) INGEMMET recommends: 'Reubicar la zona afectada, la cual estará a cargo del los evaluadores del riesgo de Defensa Civil de la Región San Martín.'

lead.evidence: not stated in sources consulted (INGEMMET only recommends relocation, to be handled by San Martín regional Civil Defence risk evaluators)

cases.notes: The cited source (Lavell et al. 2015, UCL/FLACSO diagnostic PDF) sits behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be read, by WebFetch or curl. The only source I could read is the INGEMMET technical report (June 2009) on the Shamboyacu landslide. It documents the hazard and recommends relocation but says nothing about the destination 'El Mirador' or how the move was carried out. The process and outcome variables are therefore unknown.

year_start.evidence: 'Erosion and a threat of storm flooding from the Chukchi Sea led to its relocation to higher ground in the mid-1970s.'

trigger.evidence: 'Erosion and a threat of storm flooding from the Chukchi Sea led to its relocation to higher ground in the mid-1970s.'

lead.evidence: not stated in sources consulted (search snippets mention North Slope Borough assistance, but I could not verify this in a readable source)

distance.evidence: not stated in sources consulted (an unverified search snippet said '2 miles')

hazard_at_destination.evidence: GAO 2003 on the present site: 'the runway was inoperable for 5 days last year because of flooding'; officials estimate 'between 5 to 8 feet of land are lost to erosion annually'. EWN: 'annual erosion rates greater than three feet per year in some areas... are threatening... the only road in and out of the town.'

overall.evidence: EWN: 'the community of Point Hope relocated away from the immediate coast during the mid-1970s' [para: this bought planning time], but the current site is now threatened by erosion, permafrost thaw and sea-level rise.

cases.notes: I could not access the cited Ristroph (2017) full text; ResearchGate and ScienceDirect returned 403. A search snippet attributes to Ristroph that houses were moved on runners and that the county-level government (North Slope Borough) built some facilities at the new site. I did not code this because I could not verify it. The USACE erosion paper also returned 403.

year_start.evidence: not stated; 'several households had already moved inland themselves in recent years'

households.evidence: Village population ~300; moves described only as 'several households had already moved inland themselves in recent years to "safe land up high"'

trigger.evidence: 'Karoko village (population ∼300) has lost several meters of coastland in recent years and waves reach homes and infrastructure during high tide.' ... 'ad hoc relocation has occurred as villagers move further inland due to coastal erosion.'

lead.evidence: 'In all four villages, residents themselves proposed relocation and retreat'; a resident: 'I relocated myself. My house is now on that side [pointing inland]'. No government support is reported, so this is self-organised household retreat, not community action backed by government.

single_owner.evidence: 'There are no plans for nationally-supported relocation, yet ad hoc relocation has occurred as villagers move further inland due to coastal erosion.'

resident_site_choice.evidence: 'I relocated myself. My house is now on that side [pointing inland]'; households moved 'to "safe land up high"'

tenure_destination.evidence: not stated for Karoko (the paper refers to mataqali land only for the other villages)

hazard_at_destination.evidence: not stated for the inland sites (the village as a whole 'still floods at high-tide')

cases.notes: Coded from McMichael & Katonivualiku (2020), full text read via the mobt3ath mirror. Karoko had no planned relocation. Individual households moved inland on their own, and in 2016 USAID C-CAP built a 210 m rock-mattress revetment. This is ad hoc household retreat, not a planned community relocation.

year_start.evidence: Floods 'survenues à intervalles rapprochés, en 2004, 2008 et 2009'; 'À Aoulef, 1 013 habitations ont été touchées par ces intempéries' [para: the January 2009 floods]

households.evidence: 'À Aoulef, 709 ménages ont bénéficié de la première formule (logements à 1 million de dinars), dans le cadre de l'autoconstruction'; 'À Aoulef, les 200 logements sociaux programmés sont de type F3 dans des immeubles de trois étages'

trigger.evidence: 'À Aoulef, 1 013 habitations ont été touchées par ces intempéries'

lead.evidence: [para] Rehousing was decided and delivered by the wilaya services and local authorities through state aid formulas and programmed social housing. 'Les autorités locales ont été prises de court par les stratégies élaborées et mises en œuvre par les sinistrés.'

single_owner.evidence: not clearly stated [para: wilaya services, local authorities and central state are all mentioned]

funding.evidence: Two formulas: a 1 million DA self-build grant ('709 ménages ont bénéficié de la première formule (logements à 1 million de dinars)') and state social housing ('les 200 logements sociaux programmés')

distance.evidence: [para] The social housing units were built in new buildings on the periphery of the town

return_to_origin.evidence: Return to the ksar and renting out of units are documented for Timimoun, not for Aoulef

overall.evidence: 'À Aoulef, ces opérations ont été fortement critiquées par des associations locales défendant le patrimoine'; 'Dans un centre comme Aoulef, près de la moitié (43,5 %) des bénéficiaires de l'aide ne l'ont pas utilisée'; 'À Aoulef, près de 60 % (58,6 %) des relogés se plaignent de l'exigüité des logements'

cases.notes: OpenEdition blocks direct download (Anubis bot filter), so I extracted quotes through targeted WebFetch prompts. Direct quotes are short sentences as returned by the fetch model and should be spot-checked against the article. The overall judgement leans negative. I coded it mixed because the author gives no explicit verdict of failure.

year_start.evidence: [para] Ideas date to the 1990s; formal planning began in 2010 when community leaders set up a committee to organise the relocation. The move was completed in June 2024.

households.evidence: 'Approximately 300 families relocated from Gardí Sugdub, which had housed "almost 1,300 Indigenous Guna people"' [para]

trigger.evidence: [para] Relocation responds to overcrowding and sea-level rise ('The Sea Is Eating the Land Below Our Homes')

lead.evidence: [para] Community leaders created a committee in 2010 to organise relocation; the site land was donated by community members; MIVIOT built the housing from 2017.

single_owner.evidence: [para] Three ministries (MIVIOT housing, MEDUCA school, MINSA health) each handled parts; no single coordinating body; budget problems ('lack of a budget item to pay the contractor').

resident_site_choice.evidence: 'The identified land was selected because it was available, at a safer higher elevation, and close to services' [para: land donated by community members]

tenure_destination.evidence: not explicitly stated in sources consulted (land donated by community members)

hazard_binding.evidence: 'MIVIOT required an environmental impact assessment of the relocation site in 2017. However, it did not include comprehensive evaluation of hazard risk.'

funding.evidence: [para] An IDB loan (2012) financed the school; MIVIOT committed housing construction from its budget in 2017, with repeated budget-related delays.

distance.evidence: The island sat '1,200 metres off the northern coast of Panama'; the new settlement is on the adjacent mainland [para]

hazard_at_destination.evidence: No hazard impact at Isber Yala reported in sources consulted

return_to_origin.evidence: HRW: 'many families intend to split up across two homes' and some plan to 'commute back and forth between sites'; LAB: one resident 'decided to continue running her business on the island'.

livelihoods.evidence: [para] Fishers face longer, costlier trips to fishing grounds; access to mainland agricultural plots may improve.

overall.evidence: Celebrated by the Sáhila as 'a day to celebrate for our community', but 'There was still no sustainable procedure for waste disposal, the school had no water, and the health centre had to be abandoned due to deterioration'; homes lacked space for hammocks.

cases.notes: Coded for Gardi Sugdub, whose destination was known as La Barriada and later named Isber Yala. Ukupseni (Playón Chico) has no implemented relocation. Sources describe it as a community that intends to relocate but lacks a clear plan (Mongabay 2025). The Displacement Solutions 2017 PDF link returned 404. HRW passages marked [para] come from WebFetch summaries; direct quotes should be spot-checked.

year_start.evidence: After the 17 Oct 2012 huayco, President Humala: 'Tenemos que plantear la reubicación de las familias, trabajar por la infraestructura de la zona, y lograr el restablecimiento de los caminos y del puente.'

households.evidence: Damage figures only: '12 viviendas destruidas y 6 viviendas afectadas'; 10 dead, 10 missing

trigger.evidence: 'La activación de la quebrada Umazapa, ocasionó un huayco en el caserío de El Porvenir'; relocation proposed afterwards

lead.evidence: Relocation announced by the national President after inspecting the damage ('Tenemos que plantear la reubicación de las familias...'); the regional government commissioned a risk estimate

hazard_binding.evidence: A GORE San Martín 'Estimación de riesgo del centro poblado Nuevo Porvenir' exists (2012) but its link to destination selection is not stated

cases.notes: The cited Lavell et al. (2015) PDF is blocked by Cloudflare. Sources confirm the October 2012 Umazapa debris flow and the President's call to relocate families. I found no source confirming that the relocation was carried out, or where to.

year_start.evidence: 'Following the 1994 flood disaster, Allakaket developed a comprehensive plan with the assistance of federal and state agencies for gradually relocating the village to a nearby elevated site.'

households.code: 15 HUD homes moved immediately (plus 13 temporary homes; later a second HUD subdivision)
households.evidence: 'Allakaket relocated 15 newer HUD homes to the site immediately after the disaster, and has since added a second subdivision of HUD homes.' 'Allakaket received $919,191 to build 13 temporary homes and extend its road, power, and telephone services to higher ground.'

lead.evidence: 'Allakaket developed a comprehensive plan with the assistance of federal and state agencies'; 'Officials plan to gradually migrate the entire village to the elevated site by building all new homes and infrastructure there'

single_owner.evidence: [para] Pieces came from different programmes: FEMA Hazard Mitigation Grant Program funds for temporary homes and utilities, HUD homes, and assistance from several federal and state agencies. GAO notes there is no single comprehensive federal relocation programme.

hazard_binding.evidence: Destination chosen as 'a nearby elevated site' / 'higher ground'; no formal hazard assessment described

funding.evidence: FEMA HMGP grant ('$919,191 to build 13 temporary homes...') plus HUD housing ('a second subdivision of HUD homes')

distance.evidence: 'gradually relocating the village to a nearby elevated site'

return_to_origin.evidence: not stated; migration is gradual and incomplete (plan to move 'by building all new homes and infrastructure there')

cases.notes: The origin name 'Allakeet' is taken as Allakaket, Alaska. This was a gradual, partial relocation to higher ground after the 1994 Koyukuk River flood. Neighbouring Alatna relocated separately. A 2025 flood hit Allakaket (Alaska's News Source), but I did not verify whether the elevated subdivision was affected, so I did not code it.

year_start.evidence: 'In 1981, the town was relocated just off Palo Verde Road, ¼ mile south of Interstate 10, about 8 miles north of Allenville.' [para: after the March 1978 Gila River flood]

households.evidence: [para] The plan called for 20 houses, spaces for 20 mobile homes, a community centre and park, and land for churches, a lodge and a commercial area

trigger.evidence: 'In 1978, the Gila River flooded, devastating the Allenville community'

lead.evidence: [para] Governor Babbitt declared a disaster and the Army Corps of Engineers evaluated channelisation, a dam/levee, or relocating the whole town; relocation followed via a land swap.

tenure_destination.evidence: [para] Land swap: homeowners received fair market value, and renters could buy their trailers for a 'nominal fee' and move them to Hopeville

hazard_at_destination.evidence: [para] A 2016 monsoon caused extensive trailer damage and destroyed homes in Hopeville

return_to_origin.evidence: 'The community was abandoned after it was ravaged by another flood in 1981.'

overall.evidence: [para] Hopeville struggled: the community centre burned in 2016, the lodge and commercial area never materialised, and 'the essence of Allenville was lost when the entire community did not choose to relocate to Hopeville'.

cases.notes: I could not access Perry & Lindell (1997), the cited source, or the 2001 Tucson Citizen article (connection refused). The Elementa 'lost history of managed retreat' paper returned 403. Process variables such as resident participation, which Perry & Lindell likely discuss, are therefore unknown.

year_start.evidence: 'Gemendhoo was completely abandoned after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami.' 'Most of the island's population moved to Kudahuvadhoo, the capital of the atoll.'

households.evidence: [para] Before the tsunami the island had approximately 500 inhabitants

trigger.evidence: 'Gemendhoo was completely abandoned after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami.'

return_to_origin.evidence: 'Years after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami, the island remains in its ruins, mostly visited for picnics, collection of coconuts, and palm leaves etc.'

livelihoods.evidence: not stated (pre-tsunami livelihoods: fishing and thatch production for nearby resorts)

cases.notes: The cited source (Magnan & Duvat 2014, a book) is not accessible. Search snippets said 109 houses were built on Kudahuvadhoo in two phases (50 in July 2006, 59 in July 2007), attributed to an IFRC 4-year review. I did not read that 50-page PDF, so I did not code these figures. Maldives Independent lists Gemendhoo among four islands 'permanently abandoned' after the tsunami.

year_start.evidence: Table 1, Case Study 1 (Landslide, Nuwara Eliya District, Hanguranketha DSD): 'Time period 2007–2009'

trigger.evidence: 'three post-disaster relocation projects in Sri Lanka' ... 'affected by tsunami, landslides and floods'; Case Study 1 disaster type 'Landslide'

lead.evidence: 'only a very limited number of recipients stated that they were granted the opportunity to engage in the process or had been consulted' (all three projects); funding approach 'Owner Driven'

resident_site_choice.evidence: 'when questioned about their level of engagement during the planning and design stages of the case study projects, only a very limited number of recipients stated that they were granted the opportunity to engage in the process or had been consulted'

funding.evidence: Only 'Funding approach: Owner Driven' is given; the funding source is not stated

return_to_origin.evidence: 'several houses had already been sold or rented by the first owners. In some cases, they had moved back to their original settlements... Only 21% and 27% of relocatees had moved away from the Hanguranketha and Akmeemana settlements, respectively.'

livelihoods.evidence: 'all respondents in all three case studies were dissatisfied with the space available to carry out livelihood activities (a mean value 2.17 in Hanguranketha...)'; reasons for leaving included 'distance to livelihood activities'

overall.evidence: 'resettled communities in all three case studies were mildly satisfied in the long term'; Hanguranketha overall satisfaction mean 2.93 (cut-off 2.5); 'Although the level of satisfaction was positive relating to many of the aspects, it was not strong in the majority.'

cases.notes: Full text read. The paper covers physical housing performance. It does not describe governance, land or site selection for the Hanguranketha project.

year_start.evidence: The ARAP for Micolo is dated 2020; the 2024 PAD says SEZ foundations were 'expected be established at the end of WACA ResIP (June 2024)'. The actual start of moves is not stated.

households.evidence: Programme-wide only: 'the construction of the 202 houses for the population who decided to retreat' across seven communities

trigger.evidence: 'a new study revealing shoreline loss rates approaching 0.3-2 meters / year, has led to a new urgency in the need to help the most vulnerable families with retreat management to safer adjacent areas'

lead.evidence: 'This situation occurred several times, which led the community to the request an intervention to the Central Government.' 'Planned retreat, which people can choose on a voluntary basis'; houses built 'through community-led activities'

single_owner.evidence: 'The PMU will be the entity responsible for providing all compensations to the PAP'; 'in the areas of expansion, the districts will install social infrastructure'; land issues go to district authorities; Ministry of Agriculture sets crop compensation

resident_site_choice.evidence: 'This process was done with the person affected, the representative of the Regional Government plus the members of the Community Risk Management Committee. Based on the community's Coastal Zoning Plan, the plots and areas proposed for the urbanization zone was identified.' PAD: 'Occupation and development plans have been developed in a participatory fashion for each SEZ.'

tenure_destination.evidence: 'The project intends to designate the land in the expansion area as urban land, and to allocate the plots to the families at higher risk, which would be granted title.' (planned)

hazard_binding.evidence: 'SEZ areas were identified based on a suitability assessment, which included flood modeling analysis, and criteria such as community proximity and land availability.'

funding.evidence: 'The IDA grant of the parent project is financing the preparation of the safer expansion areas... as well as the construction of the 202 houses' (a donor project, which fits none of the codebook categories cleanly)

distance.evidence: 'retreat management to safer adjacent areas'; expansion area 'located in the community of Micolo'

hazard_at_destination.evidence: not stated (relocation not yet completed in sources consulted)

return_to_origin.evidence: not stated; the ARAP plans that 'The areas of greatest risk will be designated as common green spaces, to discourage new construction.'

overall.evidence: PAD 2024: 'additional investment is required to transform these areas into growth poles' (no outcome judgement)

cases.notes: Coded mainly for Micolo, the community with the cited ARAP, within the WACA planned-retreat programme. The programme covers Santa Catarina, Micoló, Io Grande and Malanza on São Tomé, and Praia Abade and Praia das Burras on Príncipe. The Micolo ARAP deals with one person's crop losses on the expansion site and involves no physical displacement. It is a planned, not yet completed, relocation, so the outcomes are unknown. I did not read the 2018 PAD. I read the 2024 PAD for the successor project, P180982.

year_start.evidence: [para] Houses turned over in July 2013 ('327 houses turned over to residents' at the 6 July turnover) after an 18-month stay in temporary shelters following Typhoon Sendong (Dec 2011)

households.evidence: 'The community currently has 568 permanent houses'; serves 'approximately 2,800 people'. SunStar: 'More than 500 families' relocated.

trigger.evidence: 'a special resettlement project located in Lumbia, Cagayan de Oro City for the TS Sendong survivors'

lead.evidence: 'reputed as the first university-led resettlement project in the world'; built on '5.3-hectare land' provided by Xavier University [para]

single_owner.evidence: [para] Led by a private university (not a public body) with city government, barangay LGU and private organisations as stakeholders. Santiago et al.: 'national and local governments as well as non-government organizations working together'.

funding.evidence: not stated in sources consulted (university land and private donors; categories do not fit)

distance.evidence: 'Xavier Ecoville is 15 kilometers away from the city' [search-result snippet]

livelihoods.evidence: Santiago et al. abstract [para]: survivors at the three sites 'still suffered from the effects of privation and displacement more than two years after the disaster'; Ecoville set up a multipurpose cooperative (XEMPCO) to restore economic activity

overall.evidence: [para] Survivors 'still suffered from the effects of privation and displacement more than two years after the disaster', but Ecoville, with higher resident involvement, 'showed potential for transforming agency-driven processes into more sustainable, owner-driven recovery'. Residents cited inadequate electricity and water.

cases.notes: I could not access the Santiago et al. (2018) full text (ScienceDirect and Academia returned 403). Its findings are coded from the abstract as reported in search results. Distance is measured to the city centre, not from each origin barangay.

trigger.evidence: [para] Sina et al. surveyed 'five selected relocation sites in Banda Aceh and Aceh Besar' following the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami; Gampong Baro is one of them

distance.evidence: not stated in a source I could read (the sample row's '5k away' is not a source quote)

cases.notes: I could not access the Sina et al. (2019) full text or the companion World Development paper; ScienceDirect, ResearchGate and Academia all returned 403. Beware name ambiguity: a 'Gampong Baro' in Banda Aceh was a Rekompak pilot village, which may be a different place from the relocated village in Sina et al., so I did not use it.

year_start.evidence: Completion date only: 'Completed in November 2016. 91.5 ha. 277 houses.'

households.evidence: 'Completed in November 2016. 91.5 ha. 277 houses.' City-wide: 'About 3,000 households destroyed by the tsunami were relocated to seven relocation points in Higashi Matsushima.'

trigger.evidence: [para] Following the 2011 tsunami, the city built seven new communities on higher ground for displaced residents (Pinter et al. 2019)

lead.evidence: Collective relocation was prioritised as 'expressed by over 80% of residents who participated in the workshops'; community centres served as implementing agencies; 'building back better means building with the community' [para]

single_owner.evidence: [para] The city planned and implemented, while the national government financed relocation under the Disaster Response Basic Law

resident_site_choice.evidence: Residents expressed views through workshops; 'over 80% of residents who participated in the workshops' supported collective relocation [para]

hazard_binding.evidence: Decisions followed 'a set of building restrictions and guidelines (by-laws on tsunami disaster prevention area)' designating areas to be kept free of structures; relocation to hilly areas. Floodlist: new site 'very compact' but 'much safer'.

funding.evidence: [para] The national government financed reconstruction under the existing Disaster Response Basic Law, which 'provided financial support' for relocation

hazard_at_destination.evidence: No hazard impact at the Nobiru hill site reported in sources consulted

overall.evidence: Presented as a good-practice case: recovery 'aligned with the people's needs and views'; Floodlist: residents moved from a 230 ha zone to a 92 ha site that is 'very compact' but 'much safer'

cases.notes: I could not access the Pinter et al. (2019) full text (Springer requires login; the UC Davis page returned 403). Governance variables come from city-wide Higashimatsushima sources, not Nobiru-specific ones. The overall 'success' code rests on promotional or good-practice sources and should be treated with caution.

year_start.evidence: not stated (relocation followed Typhoon Haiyan, Nov 2013)

households.evidence: Site-level figure for 'Gandara' not found. City-wide [search snippet]: 'More than 15 thousand households have been relocated in Tacloban North'.

trigger.evidence: [para] 'In 2013, Typhoon Haiyan decimated informal settlements in Tacloban City's coastline, and in response, the government elected to relocate thousands of households to... Tacloban North.'

lead.evidence: [para, search snippets] The city government decided to relocate informal settlers to Tacloban North; NHA committed to more than 14,000 houses; 'housing designs, mainly concrete row houses, were predetermined by the NHA'

single_owner.evidence: [para] Sites were developed by both government (NHA) and non-government organisations; Palagi & Javernick-Will find regulative and cultural-cognitive influences 'pull implementing organizations in opposite directions, particularly across the national-local divide'

distance.evidence: [search snippet] Tacloban North 'was located approximately 10 miles to the north of downtown in a rural area'

overall.evidence: [para] Livability varied across 13 sites; 'fast construction, full occupancy, and close proximity to an economic and administrative center' were necessary for overall livability

cases.notes: I could not find 'Gandara' as a Tacloban relocation site in any source I could read. Gandara is also a municipality in Samar, which may be a separate case. MDPI, Tandfonline and ScienceDirect returned 403, and the CU GPO survey report (29 MB) was too large to fetch. Codes describe the Tacloban North programme in general, rest on abstracts and search snippets, and carry low confidence. This case needs manual follow-up.

year_start.evidence: [para] The community 'relocated several times', most recently 'in the 1970s, when the community moved to its current location from "Old Site," a spot about two miles south of the current village.'

trigger.evidence: Reason for the 1970s move not stated in sources consulted

lead.evidence: not stated for the 1970s move. The 2013-14 decision to 'defend in place' rather than relocate again was taken jointly by the Tribal Council, City Council and Village Corporation.

distance.evidence: 'moved to its current location from "Old Site," a spot about two miles south of the current village'

hazard_at_destination.evidence: Storms have 'splintered abandoned shacks, flooded septic tanks and plowed heaps of driftwood onto the ground near houses' (ADN 2014); GAO 2009 lists Shaktoolik among villages that 'will likely need to relocate all at once'

overall.evidence: No judgement of the 1970s move. A further relocation (potential site 'approximately 8.5 miles northeast of the existing village') was studied but abandoned for 'defend in place' on cost grounds ('it would have cost too much money for us').

cases.notes: Coded as the 1970s move from Old Site to the current, hazard-exposed spit. After GAO 2009, a proposed second relocation to Christmas Mountain (8.5 miles NE) was not carried out; the community chose to 'defend in place' with a berm built from 2014. I could not access Hamilton et al. (2016).
